contour_push.description: Independent adjacency message-passing boundary graph with outer/inner loops, target/goal/neighbor/tool roles, learned proximity-biased attention, global robot-state path, causal GRU and seven-command mixture head. No alphabet IDs, replay, inverse kinematics or scripted pushing.

visual_push.description: Independent trainable marked-third/detail, wrist and masked-RGB/foreground-goal convolutional encoders, state fusion, sparse causal fifteen-row-span GRU and seven-command mixture head. Shared third-view weights across scales only; no motor or perception-network weights shared with contour_push.

preprocessing.cuts: frozen cut_v3, all 22 original intervals unchanged
preprocessing.paired_rows: original indices only, no timestamp realignment or fabricated terminal row
preprocessing.native_action_source: finite action_json.dq only, retained in float64 cache
preprocessing.chart: 1280x720 Brown-Conrady undistorted using calibration K unchanged
preprocessing.perception: deterministic warm-material chroma components with neutral-surround evidence; forward Hungarian tracking; no alphabet lookup or weights
preprocessing.goal_labels: verbatim frozen original-pixel boxes at stop-1; foreground isolated before undistortion; track identity association does not revise current features
preprocessing.invalid_rows: explicit coverage accounting by precedence: supervision, command, goal, perception, required state or timing
preprocessing.context: edge exclusions may be causal context within their original cut; future auxiliary uses only fully eligible intervals
preprocessing.normalization: loss-weighted native-command and state statistics saved in metadata and model buffers
preprocessing.sampling: positive elapsed-time weights with equal per-episode physical-referent mass, divided among that referent's calls
preprocessing.cache: numeric arrays, approximately 5.5 GB; RGB decoded once per current row during preparation, with anchor-only rereads; no update-time image decoding
preprocessing.augmentation: bounded boundary extraction noise; past-frame dropout; consistent current/reference photometry and separate wrist exposure; no physical scene rotation or relabeled goal
preprocessing.tool: project recorded T_base_ee directly; do not apply TCP offset twice; image-edge support is a weak confidence cue, not a tool-width or contact calibration

dependencies: Python with torch, numpy, cv2 and scipy.optimize, plus read-only real_robot.policy_training.public. All neural components are trained from scratch. No downloaded weights, external model packages, pretrained assets or additional licenses are assumed; the environment supplies library versions listed in INTERFACE.md.
adaptations: The unavailable generic learned instance/flow models are explicitly replaced by executable class-free warm-chroma foreground proposals and forward geometric/appearance association. This removes the pretrained-segmentation asset assumption but restricts observability to separated, contrasting warm-material pieces; it is not generic arbitrary-material segmentation. Graphs cap variable loop counts at 192 nodes and preserve separate adjacency per hole/instance. Physical workspace is enforced as a caller image-polygon gate rather than claimed metric graph geometry. The visual policy uses smaller cached resolutions and five sparse frames over a fifteen-row causal span for a 24-GiB GPU, with selected/tool detail in a separate crop and the whole wrist field rather than an unverified tool-centered wrist crop. Goal RGB is foreground-isolated in a full-chart stream rather than using a future scene or an independently high-resolution goal crop. Tool projection is weak image-supported point geometry; no silhouette width or metric clearance is invented. Online geometric goal agreement is reported separately from completed withdrawal or word success.
limitations: Both policies are scientific candidates trained independently for the fixed 20000 updates, not validated robot skills. No preliminary semantic/performance study, held-out result, robot rollout, character recognizer or open-alphabet training is claimed. The HLA owns semantic interpretation, instance choice, layout and sequencing. Missing/ambiguous tracks and failed anchors are counted and refused rather than filled from future frames; excluded motion is not claimed trained. Small image-similarity goals are approximate; large perspective or metric goals require commissioned plane geometry. Tool clearance, safety limits and controller units/order/timing are unverified recording dependencies. The decoder requires explicit commissioned and current-action-bound safety attestations and performs no hardware IO. New shapes, words, materials, collisions, occlusions and generalization remain unproven; shared deterministic perception failures are not independent safety redundancy.
